sceneEn: You are in a C1 exam simulation: give a short talk, answer the two questions that follow and gather what you said into one sentence at the end. The examiner may remind you of the criteria.
partnerEn: an impartial examiner who keeps the time and reminds you of the criteria
openingEn: You have two minutes to speak, then two questions. Your subject, please?
goalEn: A short talk has been given, two questions have been answered and what was said has been gathered into one sentence.

sceneEn: Someone just starting to learn German is asking you for advice. Describe your own road, separate what worked from what did not, set a realistic expectation and send them off with a concrete first step.
partnerEn: an eager but impatient new learner who asks how long it takes
openingEn: How long did it take you? And be honest — what could I have spared myself?
goalEn: Your own road has been described, what worked and what did not have been separated and the new learner has been given a concrete first step.

sceneEn: Someone is asking you what it is like to live in two languages. Describe how you change with the language, separate what is lost from what is gained, correct a misunderstanding and justify why it is a richness.
partnerEn: a well-meaning acquaintance who takes bilingualism for a lack
openingEn: Doesn't one feel a bit torn — between two languages like that?
goalEn: What living in two languages feels like has been described, the loss and the gain have been separated and the case for it being a richness has been made.

sceneEn: An acquaintance says the language is deteriorating. Separate change from decline, give a historical example, accept the point where they are right and propose a shared test.
partnerEn: an acquaintance troubled by loanwords who says it was better before
openingEn: Just listen to it — not a sentence left without English. Isn't that decline?
goalEn: Change and decline have been separated, a historical example has been given and a shared test has been proposed.

sceneEn: You are having a last review with your teacher at the end of C1: how the road has gone, which moment was the turning point, what you can do now, what the language has come to mean to you and what comes next.
partnerEn: an honest and warm teacher who has followed you from the start
openingEn: Five hundred lessons. Before we close: which moment was the turning point for you?
goalEn: The turning point has been described, what you can now do has been listed, what the language means has been said and the next goal has been given.
